raw_findings.message: Because `init` is permissionless, any account can front-run the intended setup and permanently choose the seller, reserve, duration, and increment.
The unchecked timestamp addition and conversion to `uint64` can wrap or truncate a large duration, producing an incorrect end time while the corresponding `endBlock` may be practically unreachable.
Dividing `highestBid` before multiplying rounds the increment down prematurely, so a 500-bps increment can be zero for bids below 10,000 wei and equal bids can outbid the leader.
A top bidder whose receive hook reverts makes this refund fail, reverting every later bid and preventing the auction from being outbid.
When a bidder is outbid, their `bidOf` entry is not cleared, so they can later cancel and withdraw the already-refunded amount a second time.
Every early bid appends another entry for the same address, allowing a bidder who raises their bid repeatedly to gain multiple raffle chances.
Cancelling the current highest bid leaves `highestBidder` and `highestBid` unchanged, so the bidder can withdraw the escrow and the auction still treats that bid as payable at finalization.
The external payment occurs before `pendingReturns` is cleared, allowing a recipient that re-enters `withdraw` to receive the same pending balance repeatedly.
`finalize` never records that payment occurred or clears the winning amount, so it can be called repeatedly to pay the same bid again from bonus funds or other auction balances.
The raffle winner is derived from public block timestamp and `prevrandao`, which a block producer or transaction submitter can predict or influence when timing a draw to win the pool.

fixed_raw_findings.message: Bids are rejected as soon as `endTime` passes, so the documented 15-minute late-bid grace period is never available.
The only account with a nonzero `bidOf` is the highest bidder, but this check forbids that bidder from cancelling, making `cancelBid()` unusable.
`hasEnded()` checks only the timestamp and ignores `endBlock`, so the documented block-based fallback cannot end the auction when timestamp-based timing is unreliable.
If the configured seller rejects ETH, this push payment fails and reverts finalization, leaving no alternative way to release the winning bid.
The bonus is always paid to `earlyBidders[0]`, so the documented raffle among early bidders is not performed and the winner is predictable.
If the deterministically selected first bidder rejects ETH, the bonus transfer reverts and the pool cannot be paid to another winner.

raw_findings.message: Anyone can call `init` first and permanently choose the seller and auction parameters, so an attacker can front-run deployment setup and take control of the auction.

The unchecked cast truncates `block.timestamp + duration_` to 64 bits, so a sufficiently large duration wraps `endTime` while `endBlock` remains extremely far away and the auction cannot reach `hasEnded()`.
Dividing `highestBid` before multiplying by `minIncrementBps` rounds the increment down prematurely, allowing bids below the intended minimum and even equal bids when `highestBid < 10_000` wei.

This accepts bids through `endTime + LATE_BID_GRACE` even after `hasEnded()` becomes true at `endTime`, so a bid can be accepted after finalization and alter the recorded winner without being included in the seller payout.
The refund calls the previous bidder before updating the highest-bid state, allowing a callback to reenter `bid` against stale auction state and produce inconsistent bid accounting.
A top bidder whose receive function reverts makes every subsequent bid revert here, allowing a bidder to block the auction from advancing.
Outbidding a bidder leaves their `bidOf` amount recorded even though it was refunded, so that bidder can later cancel and withdraw the same amount again from other auction funds.
Cancelling a current top bid leaves `highestBidder` and `highestBid` unchanged, so the bidder can withdraw the bid while finalization still pays that amount to the seller.
The pending balance is cleared only after the external payment, so a receiver can reenter `withdraw` and receive the same pending amount repeatedly while funds remain.
Finalization never records that it has already occurred or clears `highestBid`, so anyone can call it repeatedly and pay the seller again from bonus funds or other balances held by the contract.
If the configured seller is a contract that rejects Ether, `finalize` always reverts and there is no pull-payment alternative to settle the auction.
The winner is derived from public block fields, so bidders can predict the index and selectively trigger the draw in a block where one of their entries wins.
If the selected early bidder is a contract that rejects Ether, the draw reverts and the pool cannot be paid or redrawn to another winner.

raw_findings.message: Because `init` is permissionless, an attacker can call it first with themselves as seller and permanently set the auction parameters before the intended initializer.
The unchecked addition followed by a `uint64` cast can truncate a large duration into an end time in the past, causing an auction initialized with that duration to end immediately.

Dividing `highestBid` before multiplying by the increment rounds the increment down in 10,000-wei chunks, so bids below 10,000 wei can be outbid with an equal amount even when a positive increment is configured.

The refund calls the previous bidder before updating auction state, allowing a bidder contract to reenter `bid` while the old highest bid is still recorded and trigger nested refunds or corrupt bid accounting.
A top bidder whose fallback rejects ETH makes this refund revert, so no competing bidder can replace them and the auction can be blocked.
When a bidder is outbid, their old `bidOf` amount is not cleared, so they can later cancel and withdraw that amount after already receiving the immediate refund.
Cancelling the current highest bid credits it for withdrawal without clearing `highestBidder` or `highestBid`, allowing finalization to pay the seller using funds the bidder has already withdrawn.
Because `pendingReturns` is cleared only after the external payment, a recipient can reenter `withdraw` and collect the same pending balance repeatedly while funds remain.

`hasEnded` becomes true just after the original end time even though `bid` still accepts bids for the 15-minute grace period, so the auction can be finalized and then accept further bids during that grace period.
`finalize` never records that payment occurred, so anyone can call it repeatedly after the auction ends and pay the same highest bid to the seller multiple times from other contract funds.
The winner is derived from public block values that a block producer can influence and callers can observe before drawing, allowing the bonus winner to be predicted or manipulated.
